# agentcss

> A mobile-web CSS component library with a machine-readable contract: 40 components,
> design tokens (light/dark), RTL and forced-colors support. No build step, no framework,
> zero third-party runtime dependency. **Class names are the API.**

Query the contract instead of guessing:

- `ai/components.json` — id, tier, maturity, root class, slots, variants, states, ARIA, file paths
- `ai/pitfalls.json` — known failure modes, keyed by component
- `ai/pitfalls-writing.json` — failure modes of prose/demos/publishing (no component key)
- `ai/tokens.json` · `ai/tokens.tree.json` — DTCG tokens, light + dark
- `ai/behaviors.json` — five behaviour cores (Esc / focus return / roving / typeahead / scroll lock)

## CLI (works without installing)

```bash
npx agentcss ai components --json                    # all 40 components
npx agentcss ai components --json --maturity=stable  # only stable
npx agentcss ai tokens --json --set=dark
npx agentcss ai pitfalls --json --component=table
npx agentcss ai validate ai/components.json --schema=components --json
npx agentcss ai check page.json --profile=strict --json
npx agentcss ai check page.html --json               # check the page you actually wrote
npx agentcss ai scaffold report/finance --out report.html   # minimal shell (skeleton, no content)
npx agentcss ai shot page.html --out shot-{width}.png --width=390,1440 --full
                                                    # PNG at exact viewport widths
npx agentcss ai pdf page.html --out page.pdf --max-pages=8 --ready-selector="#report-ready"
                                                    # waits for load + fonts + visible async content;
                                                    # zero deps; failed renders preserve an old PDF
```

`check <doc.json>` and `check <page.html>` answer **different** questions: the JSON one
validates the *plan* (node kinds, component maturity, paper obligations), the HTML one
validates the *artifact* — class names that the library does not define, stylesheets that
were never linked, missing `img alt` / table name / `th scope`, skipped heading levels,
and the per-layout obligations in `ai/recipes.json`. Both are static: no network, no browser.

`shot` drives your installed Chrome over a debugging pipe (no port, no bundled browser) so
the viewport is **exactly** the width you asked for, and reports horizontal overflow plus
JS errors. Same machine + same flags ⇒ byte-identical PNG (that is what the gate checks).

Print / PDF: `--medium=paper` is the obligation switch — only then are `printPolicy`
and `pageBudget` enforced. Per-component paper behaviour lives in
`ai/components.json` → `printPolicy`. `@page` is owned by the exporter, not the library.

Every subcommand accepts `--json`. On failure it prints *one* JSON document —
`{"ok":false,"command":"…","error":{"kind":"…","message":"…"}}` — and exits non-zero,
so a pipeline can never mistake an error for data. There is exactly one failure shape;
the `kind` values map to exit codes: `1` verdict-negative (`findings`), `2` bad usage,
`3` environment missing, `4` render failed, `5` over budget, `6` tool bug.

Enum flags (`--set`, `--cat`, `--maturity`, `--profile`, `--medium`, `--recipe`) reject
an unknown value, an empty value, and a repeated occurrence with exit `2`. Flags a
subcommand does not understand are rejected too — they are never silently ignored.

`pitfalls` needs `agentcss@0.21.0+`: `npx` resolves the *published* version, which can lag
this repository. If a subcommand is missing, check `npx agentcss --version` first.

There is **no MCP server**: the CLI is the whole interface (no daemon, no network,
no second copy of the contract to keep in sync). `scaffold` and `shot` write only the file
you name; every other subcommand is a read-only query. See `ai/START-HERE.md` §7.

## Use it in a page

1. `<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/agentcss/dist/01-tokens/tokens.css">`
2. add `typography.css` / `page.css` only if you use the page skeleton
3. add the component's own CSS, then copy its markup from `demo.html`
4. restyle with tokens (CSS variables); do not rewrite component selectors

## Rules that prevent most breakage

- **Copy markup from `demo.html`** — it is the ground truth, not the prose.
- 44×44 px minimum touch target; `:focus-visible` only, never `outline: 0`.
- Every state must stay readable without colour — forced-colors drops backgrounds.
- Tables and other wide content need their own scroll container.
- Behaviour (drawer / tabs / overlay) needs its JS; the CSS alone is not interactive.

**Language:** prose docs (component READMEs, demos) are Chinese; JSON keys, CLI flags and this file are English.
